title: Ensure all default accounts are either disabled or utilize strong passwords
description: Disable the known default accounts configured. Note: The default admin account must remain enabled for high availability synchronization to work. Disabling it could cause issues. Default accounts are accounts with predefined usernames and passwords that are typically included with software and hardware devices. Attackers often target default accounts because they are widely known and can be used to gain unauthorized access to a system. To prevent unauthorized access, all default accounts should either be disabled or have their passwords changed.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure all default accounts are either disabled or utilize strong passwords

audit.command: In GUI: - Navigate to System > Access > Users - View the default users

remediation.command: In GUI: - Navigate to System > Access > Users - Remove any default users that are not used. Note: The default admin account must remain enabled for high availability synchronization to work. Disabling it could cause issues.

title: Ensure Web Management is Set to use HTTPS
description: Web Admin Management Portal should only be accessed using HTTPS Protocol. HTTP transmits all data (including passwords) in clear text over the network and provides no assurance of the identity of the hosts involved. Because of this HTTP should never be used for sensitive tasks such as managing network devices or entering login credentials and HTTPS should be configured for Web Portal Management instead
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.8 Ensure Web Management is Set to use HTTPS

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System -> Settings -> Administration - Select the 'Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security' option - Click 'Save'

title: Ensure LDAP or RADIUS server configured
description: Configured the LDAP Servers or Radius server for central authentication. Authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA) scheme provide an authoritative source for managing and monitoring access for devices.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure LDAP or RADIUS server configured

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System > Access > Servers - Click the Orange Plus sign in the top right - Enter the details needed for your LDAP server - Click 'Save' at the bottom

title: Ensure Console Menu is Password Protected
description: Set the Console Menu to password protected. An unattended computer with an open Console Menu session to the device could allow an unauthorized user access to the firewall’s management.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure Console Menu is Password Protected

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System > Settings > Administration - Scroll to the 'Console' Section - Ensure 'Password protect the console menu' is checked - Click 'Save'

title: Ensure Default Deny is Enforced on All Internal Interfaces
description: You must enforce a default deny policy on all internal interfaces (e.g., LAN, VLANs, DMZ, VPN). Default deny prevents accidental exposure and limits lateral movement.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.1 Ensure Default Deny is Enforced on All Internal Interfaces

remediation.command: - Navigate to Firewall → Rules - Verify each internal interface contains only explicit allow rules and no broad “any/any” permits. - Confirm traffic not explicitly allowed is denied. - Remove broad allow rules. - Replace with explicit allow rules using aliases.

title: Ensure Least Privilege is Applied to All Permit Rules
description: All allow rules must restrict traffic by: - Source - Destination - Protocol - Port/service Overly broad rules create hidden attack paths.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.2 Ensure Least Privilege is Applied to All Permit Rules

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Identify allow rules with: - Source = any - Destination = any - Port = any 3. Validate business justification exists. 4. Replace broad rules with alias-driven scoped rules.

title: Ensure “Any → Any” Rules are Prohibited
description: You must not deploy any rule that permits “any source → any destination → any port.” This defeats segmentation and enables unrestricted lateral movement.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.3 Ensure “Any → Any” Rules are Prohibited

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules → [All interfaces] 2. Identify rules where: - Source = any - Destination = any - Destination port = any

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules → [All interfaces] 2. Identify rules where: - Source = any - Destination = any - Destination port = any 3. Remove the rule. - Replace with explicit rules using aliases.

title: Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used
description: Although IPv6 has many advantages over IPv4, not all organizations have IPv6 or dual stack configurations implemented. If IPv6 or dual stack is not to be used, it is recommended that IPv6 be disabled to reduce the attack surface of the system.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Ensure IPv6 is disabled if not used

remediation.command: In the GUI: Navigate to Interfaces -> Settings Uncheck 'Allow IPv6'

title: Ensure 'Disable DNS Rebinding Checks' is unchecked
description: Ensure that the 'Disable DNS Rebinding Checks' is unchecked to protect against DNS rebinding attacks. Attackers can use DNS rebinding to exploit a DNS server's response to a domain name query that resolves to a private IP address. This could provide a hacker access to private network resources that shouldn't be made available to the general public. To defend against this kind of attack, OPNsense's "DNS Rebind Check" function disables private IP responses from DNS servers. As advised in the CIS benchmark, disabling this feature would expose the system to DNS rebinding attacks.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure 'Disable DNS Rebinding Checks' is unchecked

remediation.command: In the GUI - Navigate to System -> Settings -> Administration - uncheck the 'Disable DNS Rebinding Checks' Field - Click save

title: Ensure Sessions Timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 Minutes
description: The session inactivity timeout setting represents the amount of time a user can be inactive before the user's session times out and closes. It only affects user browser sessions. Indefinite or even long session timeout window increase the risk of attackers abusing abandoned sessions
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure Sessions Timeout is set to less than or equal to 10 Minutes

remediation.command: In GUI: - Navigate to System > Settings > Administration - Scroll to the 'Session Timeout' - Set 10 in the 'Session Timeout' field - Click Save

title: Ensure 'Local Account status' is set to 'Disabled'
description: Disable the 'Local User' account except for the admin user. Local accounts pose a threat to system security since the users are not manageable from the LDAP server.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure 'Local Account status' is set to 'Disabled'

audit.command: Need to manually check each account.

remediation.command: Disabled Local User Account.

title: Ensure Login Protection methods are enabled.
description: OPNsense strongly recommends enabling two-factor authentication (e.g., using TOTP) to protect user accounts, which is highly effective against password-based brute-force attacks.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure Login Protection methods are enabled.

remediation.command: - Navigate to System > Access > Servers - Click the Plus Sign to add a TOTP Server - Give the server a descriptive name - Select the TOTP Server Type - Select a Token Length of 6 - Install Google Authenticator on your phone - Add a user from System > Access > Users - Enter a Username and Password and fill in the other fields just as you would do for any other user. Then select the Generate new (160bit) secret under OTP seed. - Click Save - For testing the user authentication, OPNsense offers a simple tester. Go to System ‣ Access ‣ Tester - Select the Authentication server you have configured, and enter the user name. Then enter the *token + password, remember the order is token and then password in the same field. - Hit the test button and if all goes well you should see successfully authenticated. - Per default the system validates user credentials against the “Local Database”. In System ‣ Settings ‣ Administration, section Authentication you should change this to your newly added authentication server to make sure no local user can gain access without 2FA.

title: Ensure default password of admin is changed
description: Ensure the default password is changed for the root user. Using default passwords for the 'root' account could cause a compromise to the system.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure default password of admin is changed

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System > Access > Users - Click the Pencil Icon under 'Commands' - Change the password of the default 'root' user account. - Click 'Save' at the bottom of the page.

title: Ensure Every Rule Has a Description Using a Standard Format
description: Every firewall rule must include a description using the format: <ZONE> → <DEST> : <SERVICE> (Purpose) Descriptions are required for auditability and safe change control.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.4 Ensure Every Rule Has a Description Using a Standard Format

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Verify no rule has an empty description field. 3. Verify descriptions are meaningful and standardized.

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Verify no rule has an empty description field. 3. Verify descriptions are meaningful and standardized. 4. Update any rules that do not comply 5. Save each rule

title: Ensure Aliases are Used for Hosts, Networks, and Port Groups
description: You must use aliases for: - Any host referenced more than once - Any port group referenced more than once - All VLANs / security zones Aliases reduce errors and simplify audits.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.5 Ensure Aliases are Used for Hosts, Networks, and Port Groups

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Aliases 2. Confirm: - Networks are defined as aliases - Common port groups exist (DNS, NTP, Web, AD, etc.) 3. Confirm rules reference aliases instead of raw IPs repeatedly.

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Aliases 2. Confirm: - Networks are defined as aliases - Common port groups exist (DNS, NTP, Web, AD, etc.) 3. Confirm rules reference aliases instead of raw IPs repeatedly. 4. Create aliases and update rules accordingly.

title: Ensure Rules are Implemented on the Ingress Interface
description: You must define rules on the interface where traffic enters the firewall. OPNsense evaluates rules based on ingress interface. Misplaced rules cause bypass or failure.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.6 Ensure Rules are Implemented on the Ingress Interface

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Validate each rule exists on the correct ingress interface.

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Validate each rule exists on the correct ingress interface. 3. Move rules to the correct interface, if they are on the wrong one.

title: Ensure Standard Rule Ordering is Used Per Interface
description: Rules must be ordered as follows: 1. Management / anti-lockout 2. Infrastructure (DNS/DHCP/NTP) 3. Internal access rules 4. Internet access rules 5. Explicit block rules (logged) Consistent ordering improves readability and reduces mistakes.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.7 Ensure Standard Rule Ordering is Used Per Interface

audit.command: - Navigate to Firewall → Rules → [Interface] - Confirm Ordering matches the standard

remediation.command: - Navigate to Firewall → Rules → [Interface] - Confirm Ordering matches the standard - Reorder rules that do not comply

title: Ensure Floating Rules are Restricted to Cross-Zone Policy Use Cases
description: Floating rules must be used only when: - Policy must apply across multiple interfaces - “Quick” evaluation is required Floating rules can override interface policy and cause unexpected behavior.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1.8 Ensure Floating Rules are Restricted to Cross-Zone Policy Use Cases

audit.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules → Floating 2. Validate each floating rule has: - documented justification - limited scope

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules → Floating 2. Validate each floating rule has: - documented justification - limited scope 3. Move rules to interface rulesets when possible.

title: Ensure time zone is properly configured
description: Sets the local time zone information so that the device's time display is more accurate for viewers. The device's time setting needs to be accurate for two reasons in particular. The first is that digital certificates use this time to compare the validity period they specify in their Valid From and Valid To fields to a range of times. The second justification is the need for accurate time stamps when logging data. When doing packet captures, delivering messages to a Syslog server, SNMP monitoring stations, or other tasks, timestamps are only meaningful if you can be certain of their accuracy.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1.1 Ensure time zone is properly configured

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to Services > Network Time > General - Add NTP servers under 'Time Servers' - Select one as preferred by checking 'Prefer' - Click 'Save'

title: Ensure WireGuard is used as the default VPN method
description: WireGuard must use a dedicated RFC1918 subnet that is not reused by any internal VLAN. Additionally, WireGuard must remain disabled unless explicitly required for approved remote access or site-to-site VPN use cases.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3.1 Ensure WireGuard is used as the default VPN method

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to VPN → WireGuard → Instances 2. Click the Plus Sign to add a WireGuard Instance 3. Click 'Save' when all of your instance details are entered

title: Ensure Logging is Enabled for Inter-Zone Deny Rules
description: All deny rules that enforce segmentation between VLANs/zones must have logging enabled. Inter-zone denies are high-signal and reveal lateral movement attempts.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure Logging is Enabled for Inter-Zone Deny Rules

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to Firewall → Rules 2. Identify deny rules between VLANs 3. Enable logging for segmentation deny rules.

title: Ensure Logging is Enabled for Management Plane Deny Rules
description: All deny rules targeting firewall management services or MGMT networks must be logged. Management targeting is a high-risk indicator and should generate security alerts.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure Logging is Enabled for Management Plane Deny Rules

audit.command: Verify deny rules for MGMT subnets and firewall GUI/SSH ports have logging enabled.

remediation.command: Enable logging on MGMT deny rules.

title: Ensure Remote Syslog is Configured
description: OPNsense must forward logs to a remote log server or SIEM using syslog. Local-only logs can be erased during compromise and are not sufficient for enterprise IR.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure Remote Syslog is Configured

audit.command: 1. Navigate to System → Settings → Logging / Targets (or Syslog depending on build) 2. Confirm at least one remote syslog target exists. 3. Confirm logs are received by the SIEM.

remediation.command: 1. Navigate to System → Settings → Logging / Targets (or Syslog depending on build) 2. Configure syslog target(s) to an enterprise log platform.

title: Ensure SSH warning banner is configured
description: Before authentication is allowed, a file containing its contents must be provided to the remote user, as specified by the Banner argument. Banners are used to inform users who are connected of the specific site's connection rules. The prosecution of computer system intruders may be aided by the display of a warning message prior to the normal user login.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure SSH warning banner is configured

audit.command: In the CLI: 1. Run the following command and verify that output should contain 'Banner' parameter: cat /etc/ssh/my_banner Ensure a file exists in the /etc/ssh/ directory and that it contains the information you want in your ssh banner. 2. Run the following command and verify that a file exists, and that it references the above referenced "my_banner" file via a line such as: Banner /etc/ssh/my_banner

remediation.command: In the CLI: 1. Create a banner file in the /etc/ssh/ directory via the following command vi /etc/ssh/my_banner 2. To ensure your banner remains, you should utilize OPNsense's Targeted Overlays system by creating a file in the following directory: vi /usr/local/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-custom.conf 3. Then insert the following text in the 99-custom.conf file to reference your ssh banner file: Banner /etc/ssh/my_banner Save and exit the file 4. Restart OPNsense via the gui.

title: Ensure Backup count is set to 5 or more.
description: OPNsense is able to store a user defined number of backups in a local cache. An after-the-fact backup is taken after evaluating the change and ensuring it had the intended outcome. Periodic backups are also helpful, regardless of changes, especially in cases where a manual backup may be missed.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure Backup count is set to 5 or more.

audit.command: In the GUI. - Navigate to System -> Configuration -> Backups Confirm "Backup Count" is set to 5 or more.

remediation.command: In the GUI. - Navigate to System -> Configuration -> Backups - Set the "Backup Count" to 5 or more. - Click "Save"

title: Ensure 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' is set
description: Sets the MOTD message. Network banners are electronic messages that provide notice of legal rights to users of computer networks. From a legal standpoint, banners have four primary functions. - First, banners may be used to generate consent to real-time monitoring under Title III. - Second, banners may be used to generate consent to the retrieval of stored files and records pursuant to ECPA. - Third, in the case of government networks, banners may eliminate any Fourth Amendment "reasonable expectation of privacy" that government employees or other users might otherwise retain in their use of the government's network under O'Connor v.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure 'Message Of The Day (MOTD)' is set

audit.command: In the OPNsense Shell type: cat /var/run/motd

remediation.command: In the OPNsense Shell use vi to edit the message of the day: vi /var/run/motd

title: Ensure Hostname is set
description: Changes the device default hostname. The device hostname is crucial for asset inventory and identification as a security need, as well as for the deployment of public keys and certificates and for comparing logs from various systems while handling an issue.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Ensure Hostname is set

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System > Settings -> General - Update the field 'Hostname' with the new hostname, and click "Save"

title: Ensure DNS server is configured
description: You must specify the main DNS server for your system in order to enable DNS lookups. Additionally, supplementary and third-party DNS servers can be specified. The system uses the main name server to resolve host names. The system examines the secondary name server, and if required, the tertiary, if a failure or time-out occurs. The purpose is to perform the resolution of system hostnames to Internet Protocol (IP) addresses.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure DNS server is configured

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to System -> Settings -> General - Update the field 'DNS Servers' with the Your DNS Server, and click "Save"

title: Ensure 'DNSSEC' is Enable on DNS Service
description: Enable the "DNSSEC" in the DNS Service Configuration. Enable DNSSEC Support. DNSSEC is a means of protecting DNS data from attacks which use forged or manipulated DNS data, such as DNS cache poisoning.
reference: CIS OPNsense Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2.1 Ensure 'DNSSEC' is Enable on DNS Service

audit.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to Services > Unbound DNS > General - Verify if 'Enable DNSSEC Support' is checked

remediation.command: In the GUI: - Navigate to Services > Unbound DNS > General - Check next to 'Enable DNSSEC Support' - Click 'Apply'
